images.filename: St. Anselm Parish Church (Priory Chapel), St. Louis Abbey, Mason Road, Creve Coeur, MO - Flickr - w lemay.jpg
images.caption: Built in 1960-1962, this Modern building was designed by Gyo Obata to serve as the St. Anselm Parish Church and Priory Chapel, part of St. Louis Abbey, founded in 1955.  The building is made up of a concrete thin shell structure with multiple parabolic vaults at two different levels, which contain openings with stained glass curtain walls, a central tower made up of parabolic vaults, which contains a campanile, multiple doorways at ground level, and a one-story brick-clad enclosed hallway on the south side of the building that connects it to the adjacent monastery.  Inside, the chapel features a vaulted ceiling, ample natural light, a centrally-placed granite altar beneath an oculus in the middle of the ceiling, and simple wooden pews and furnishings.  The building today serves as the St. Anselm Parish Church, as well as the Priory Chapel for St. Louis Abbey.
